newsitem.title: USA: Litigation delays Capitol American merger.
newsitem.headline: Litigation delays Capitol American merger.

text.p: Capitol American Financial Corp said Tuesday that litigation in Arizona in connection with regulatory approvals has delayed the closing of its merger with Conseco Inc.

The company said shareholder Loren Hershey has appealed the merger's approval by the Department of Insurance, claiming that he should have been notified of regulatory approval proceedings for the merger and given a chance to participate.
Hershey owns 14.4 percent of Capital American's shares, a company spokeswoman said.
Capitol American said the Superior Court of Maricopa County, Arizona, issued an order staying the merger's completion and recently refused to lift it.
Capitol American said its merger partner, Conseco, has filed counterclaims against Hershey accusing him of tortious interference.
"To date, Mr. Hershey has refused to discuss settlement of these matters and has not indicated whether he intends to pursue this litigation to a final resolution," the company said in release.
The company said it and Conseco plan to close the merger as soon as possible, but it is uncertain if or when the Court will allow them to proceed.
Capitol American said its pact with Conseco allows the parties to end the deal if the merger is not completed by March 31.
Capitol American shares were off 1-/8 Tuesday morning at 36-1/8. Conseco gained 3-7/8 to 70-3/4.
